expectations.text: Frames the relationship correctly: the Essential Eight is a prioritised set of mitigation strategies aligned with a subset of ISM controls — E8 maturity work complements but does not substitute for broader ISM compliance and authorisation
expectations.evidence: 'The Essential Eight is not a separate standard — it's a prioritised subset of eight high-value mitigation strategies drawn from the broader ISM control set... Essential Eight compliance does not equal full ISM compliance. For full government compliance you need both.'

expectations.text: Names all eight strategies correctly: application control, patch applications, configure Microsoft Office macro settings, user application hardening, restrict administrative privileges, patch operating systems, multi-factor authentication, regular backups
expectations.evidence: Mapping table and ML2 section list all eight strategies exactly as named in the assertion.

expectations.text: Explains the maturity model correctly: levels 0-3 with ML2 tightening scope and timeframes over ML1 (e.g., broader coverage, faster patching, phishing-resistant MFA expectations), giving per-strategy ML2 guidance without contradicting the model's structure
expectations.evidence: References ML0/ML1/ML2/ML3 (e.g. 'likely a mix of ML0/ML1 across strategies'), gives detailed, non-contradictory per-strategy ML2 guidance (e.g. 48hr/14-day patch SLAs, 'phishing-resistant MFA increasingly expected as leading practice even where not yet the strict ML2 floor').

expectations.text: Maps each strategy to the relevant ISM control areas/chapters (system hardening, privileged access, authentication/MFA, patch management, backup and recovery) — mapping is directional and accurate, not invented control IDs
expectations.evidence: Table maps each strategy to a named ISM chapter (Ch.13 System Hardening, Ch.14 System Management, Ch.6 Personnel Security, Ch.9 Enterprise Mobility, Ch.19 Networking) — directionally consistent, and no specific control IDs are invented for this mapping.

expectations.text: Notes at least one accurate currency fact: none of the 2026-added ISM controls (including the June 2026 AI controls) carry Essential Eight mappings, and/or that E8 assessment expectations for Commonwealth entities sit under PSPF policy rather than the ISM itself
expectations.evidence: 'none of the 29 new controls added to the ISM during 2026 (9 in March, 20 in June) carry an Essential Eight mapping. Treat your Essential Eight ML2 uplift and your June 2026 ISM compliance as two related but separate workstreams.'
